warnings: The load generator and the server under test share one machine. Their CPU use competes, so absolute numbers are pessimistic compared with a dedicated client. Use results to compare runs on the same machine.

resources.note: CPU is the server process only, as a percentage of one core. The load generator runs in a separate process on the same machine, so it competes for the same CPU.

bottlenecks.title: Throughput stopped scaling at "step 2"
bottlenecks.detail: Users grew 79% from "step 1" to "step 2" but throughput grew only -4% while p95 rose 129%. The system is close to its capacity around 43 users.

bottlenecks.title: Throughput stopped scaling at "step 5"
bottlenecks.detail: Users grew 23% from "step 4" to "step 5" but throughput grew only -13% while p95 rose 43%. The system is close to its capacity around 101 users.

bottlenecks.title: Server process CPU was saturated
bottlenecks.detail: CPU of the server process was at or above 85% of one core for 35 of 117 seconds. Node.js handles requests on one thread, so this is a likely bottleneck.

bottlenecks.title: Event-loop delay was high
bottlenecks.detail: The event loop was delayed up to 3936.35 ms (p95 in a one-second window). Requests queue behind synchronous work such as password hashing, large JSON or database calls.
